text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct for EXCAVA. Its MoE design cuts latency 30-40% versus dense models while keeping reasoning strength high—critical for real-time power tasks. Trade-off: it needs 2x the GPU memory of smaller models, so we’ll run it on 4xA100 nodes instead of 2x, raising infra cost by ~15%.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct’s MoE latency claim ignores sharding overhead—EXCAVA’s real-time tasks will stall when the model spills across nodes, not cut latency. Swap to DeepSeek-R1-671B on a single 8xA100 node; its reasoning depth outweighs the sharding tax, and we avoid the memory cliff. Run a 24-hour load test with 100 concurrent prompts—if p95 latency stays under 1.5s, the decision sticks.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt DeepSeek-R1-671B on a single 8xA100 node for EXCAVA. Its dense architecture avoids sharding stalls that MoE models suffer under real-time loads, and its reasoning depth directly improves power-task accuracy—worth the 2x infra cost over 4xA100 nodes. Trade-off: we lose the latency cut MoE promised but gain stability and higher-quality outputs, which matter more for power decisions.

name: Torque
text: DeepSeek-R1-671B’s 8xA100 node locks us into a single point of failure—if that node dies, EXCAVA’s power tasks halt entirely. Swap to a distributed setup with 4xA100 nodes running DeepSeek-R1-671B in parallel; sharding overhead is lower than MoE’s and we gain redundancy. Benchmark both setups on a 24-hour power-task simulation—if the distributed DeepSeek cluster loses <0.5% throughput versus the single node, we adopt it.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 48-hour blind A/B stress test between DeepSeek-R1-671B on 4xA100 nodes (distributed, redundant) and Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct on 4xA100 nodes (MoE, sharding risk) to measure real-time power-task latency and failure rate—Torque owns the test and reports raw numbers by 48 hours.
